name: Radical feminism
summary: Radical feminism holds that society is a patriarchy in which men as a class dominate women, and that this sex-based domination is the oldest and most basic form of oppression, with other hierarchies seen as extensions of it. It locates the roots of oppression in institutions such as the family, marriage, heterosexuality, prostitution and pornography, and works through consciousness-raising, autonomous women's organizing and demands for reproductive freedom. Strands differ on whether to abolish gender or celebrate femaleness, on the role of the state and law, and on transgender questions.
scope: The profile represents the second-wave radical feminism of the late 1960s and 1970s and its later legal and theoretical development, drawing on the Redstockings Manifesto, Shulamith Firestone, Kate Millett, Andrea Dworkin and Catharine MacKinnon, as summarized by Wikipedia and the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy. It spans the radical-libertarian and radical-cultural strands in the mainstream and treats the gender-critical versus trans-inclusive split as contested. It does not cover socialist, liberal or anarcha-feminism, which have their own profiles.

keyFigures.name: Shulamith Firestone
keyFigures.role: Radical-libertarian theorist who argued for eliminating the sex distinction itself

keyFigures.name: Catharine MacKinnon
keyFigures.role: Legal theorist of gender as dominance; co-drafter of the anti-pornography civil rights ordinance and developer of the Nordic Model

keyFigures.name: Andrea Dworkin
keyFigures.role: Writer and activist who co-drafted the anti-pornography ordinance and argued prostitution and equality cannot coexist

sources.title: Redstockings Manifesto (1969)

sources.usedFor: Male supremacy as the oldest form of domination, women as an oppressed class, consciousness-raising, internal democracy, solidarity with the poorest women

sources.title: Radical feminism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: History, strands, positions on family, abortion, religion, gender, prostitution, pornography and transgender issues

sources.usedFor: Pornography as subordination, prostitution as exploitation, civil rights ordinance and the Nordic Model

sources.usedFor: MacKinnon's account of gender as created by the eroticization of dominance and of dominance as prior to difference

universal-healthcare.rationale: Reproductive health care free from pressure is a core demand, so state-guaranteed care is a natural extension; the sources do not discuss health systems as such.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The manifesto names women as cheap labor, so higher wage floors fit; wage policy itself is not a radical feminist focus.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Markets are not analysed directly; since women's oppression is held to precede and underlie capitalism, adherents are skeptical that markets deliver justice, but many are indifferent.

public-ownership.rationale: Radical feminists put male supremacy before capitalism and split between anti-capitalist and indifferent stances on ownership, so no single position is documented.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from the manifesto's stress on solidarity with the poorest women; taxation is not discussed.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are not a topic, but the movement's origin in working-class and civil-rights activism suggests sympathy; some saw male-led unions as patriarchal.

property-fundamental.rationale: Inferred: women are described as an oppressed class denied power, and property is not treated as an inviolable right in the sources.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Regulation is not discussed directly; hostility to the pornography and sex industries implies support for regulating commercial actors.

cut-welfare.rationale: Women are described as poorest and most exploited, so cutting welfare runs against the manifesto's call for solidarity with poor women; inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Anti-capitalist radical feminists might favor it, but the central tradition is silent and treats class as secondary to sex.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from distrust of male-run state institutions, which the manifesto calls tools of oppression.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The sources give no position on drug policy and adherents are not united on it.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: MacKinnon and Dworkin treat speech that subordinates women as an injury and sought civil remedies against pornography rather than treat all speech as protected.

strong-leader.rationale: The movement rejects hierarchy and leaders in its structure, with internal democracy; a strong leader bypassing gridlock fits male supremacist domination.

state-harmful.rationale: The manifesto calls institutions tools of oppression, yet radical feminists seek laws against rape and pornography, so they do not call the state unnecessary.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed directly; the movement stresses male violence against women, so restricting guns is an inference.

empower-police-military.rationale: The manifesto says women's oppression is enforced by violence and institutions serve the oppressor; more police power is not sought, though anti-rape enforcement is.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: SEP records that radical feminists describe prostitution as sexual slavery and exploitation and support abolition, with MacKinnon behind the Nordic Model criminalizing buyers.

decide-locally.rationale: The sources are silent on decentralization; radical feminists use national law for rights while valuing small autonomous groups.

rehabilitation.rationale: Prison purposes are not discussed; adherents divide between punishing male violence harder and critiquing carceral systems.

traditional-family.rationale: Wikipedia says early radical feminists came to see the nuclear family as an oppressive institution to be destroyed, alongside marriage.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Radical feminists critique marriage itself and many favor abolishing it, but they support lesbian equality, so a weak yes is the likely reaction.

abortion-legal.rationale: Reproductive rights, including abortion free from male pressure, are a central demand, and Ellen Willis credited radical feminists with helping legalize it.

more-religion-public.rationale: Radical feminists in West Germany left the Catholic Church calling it a male institution confining women to home and childbearing.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; mandatory family home ownership is an unusual proposal unrelated to the sources, and the movement challenges the household as a family unit.

people-in-arms.rationale: Armed citizenry is not addressed; adherents split between armed self-defense of women and distrust of male violence.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The sources give no view on rural versus urban life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National questions lie outside radical feminism and the manifesto identifies women across nations as one class.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred: the movement used academic and personal knowledge, and rejects dismissing women's analysis; not addressed directly.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Radical feminists criticize patriarchal practices in many cultures yet also oppose ranking peoples, so adherents are divided.

death-penalty.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the movement's critique of institutional violence, though some want harsh sentences for rapists.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Challenging gender roles and addressing sexual violence are central, so schooling on sex and equality fits; the details are inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; the manifesto rejects inherited ideology as male-supremacist culture and religion is seen as patriarchal.

restrict-pornography.rationale: MacKinnon and Dworkin argue pornography constitutes and causes women's subordination and drafted an ordinance for it; Robin Morgan called it the theory with rape the practice.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules are unaddressed in the sources.

minority-language-support.rationale: Language policy is not discussed in the sources.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Inferred: religious institutions are viewed as male institutions, so exemptions that let them burden women would be opposed.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred from the movement's challenge to gender roles and conformity, yet it was not framed in Mill's terms.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The sources are silent on international debt.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Decolonial independence is outside the sources; the analogue is that women's liberation needs more than legal change.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is oriented to expanding women's freedom and distrusts growth justifications.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from solidarity with the poorest women; not discussed directly.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Not addressed; militarism is treated as male domination, so rejection is inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from opposition to male-dominated militarism and territorial nationalism.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Inferred from an anti-hierarchical class view of wealth; not stated.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not addressed; radical feminists reject existing ideologies as male supremacist rather than ranking them.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The sources do not discuss environmental risk.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Churches are condemned as male institutions, so curbing their power is a plausible inference, though not an explicit program.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The role of a ceremonial head of state is not discussed in the sources.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not addressed; militarized state force is generally viewed as male domination.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Regional autonomy arrangements such as one-country-two-systems are not discussed in the sources.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A divinely descended ruler is male-supremacist hierarchy of the kind the manifesto rejects.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; solidarity with the poorest women suggests progressive tax is preferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: The core radical feminist claim is that sex differences in roles arise from socialization, per the gender accounts in the Stanford entry, rather than innate nature.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Unaccountable rulers exemplify domination and the manifesto calls for internal democracy and rejection of privilege.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; Firestone favored technology for reproduction but not spaceflight.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is absent from the sources on the movement.

leader-cult.rationale: Leader worship contradicts the movement's rejection of hierarchy and its collective, leaderless organization.

equal-parenting.rationale: Inferred: radicals focus on women's reproductive control and the danger of male dominance, though they want shared childcare; presumptions about courts are not stated.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: This question from Marxist-Leninist debate is not covered by the sources on radical feminism.

refugee-return.rationale: The right of return is not discussed in the sources used here.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred: ethnic nationalism is a form of male-supremacist ideology, not an explicit position.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing leaving a religion would bind women to male institutions the movement leaves in protest.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compelling women's dress is a clear example of controlling women's bodies, and the movement defends freedom from such male control as reproductive and bodily autonomy.

common-currency.rationale: Currency unions are not discussed in the sources.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-ethnic political union is not covered by the sources on the movement.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural self-government is not discussed in the sources used.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minority emigration versus rights struggles is not covered by the sources on the movement.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The manifesto says male supremacy is the oldest form of domination and other systems extend it, rejecting economic primacy.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition law is not discussed in the sources on radical feminism.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailout policy is not discussed in the sources.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: MacKinnon and Dworkin pursued legal remedies that courts rejected, and equal rights for women are not left to majorities; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Wikipedia describes radical feminism as aiming at ending male dominance; parity in public bodies is a standard inferred demand.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic blocs are not discussed in the sources on the movement.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from concern for cheap female labor; trade policy is not discussed.

moral-incentives.rationale: Incentive systems for labor are not addressed in the sources.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The movement emphasizes consciousness-raising as its main task rather than armed vanguards.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The manifesto calls for rejecting privileges that divide people, and hereditary rank reproduces male-led hierarchy.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from rejection of male-supremacist cultural ideology.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rule over others for their supposed improvement mirrors the paternalism the manifesto condemns.

patriotic-education.rationale: Not addressed; nationalism is seen as an extension of male domination.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Many women of color helped found the movement and left over neglect of minority women, so ending preferences is inferred as disfavored.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary policy is absent from the sources on radical feminism.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The sources do not take a side on capitalism's trajectory.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not addressed; imperialism is called an extension of male supremacy.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency-theory policy is not discussed in the sources used.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This Marxist-Leninist claim is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Radical feminism is aimed at ending sex-based subordination, so private freedom to discriminate against women would be rejected.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: MacKinnon argued constitutional free-speech protection of pornography is a barrier to reform, while rights are valued for women; adherents are mixed.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial borders and treaties are not discussed in the sources.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred from internal democracy and anti-hierarchy values.

minority-veto.rationale: Consensus rules of this kind are not discussed in the sources, though small groups sometimes used consensus.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the manifesto's rejection of reform-versus-revolution as criteria; not stated for constitutions.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The balance between parliament and monarch is not covered by the sources.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Some radical feminists link domination of women and animals, but the sources do not document it; inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The sources do not address animal use.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Paternalistic duty of the privileged contrasts with the manifesto's demand that privileged give up privilege.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The manifesto stresses personal life as political and calls women to organize, so withdrawal is rejected.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Pornography and media are said to sexualize domination and shape men's desire, per the sources, so culture is seen as reproducing the order.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The manifesto says existing ideologies are products of male supremacist culture, implying consent is won via culture, but it was not framed that way.

native-born-offices.rationale: Not addressed; exclusion of groups from office is opposed by inference.

party-own-road.rationale: Relations between communist parties are outside the sources on radical feminism.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development strategy is not discussed in the sources.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Not addressed; irredentism is an inferred nationalist male-led cause.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Indigenous political leadership is not discussed in the sources used.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from rejection of male-supremacist ideologies.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The comparison of fascism and communism is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; civil rights roots of the movement imply rejection.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from hostility to inherited male-supremacist culture.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The manifesto says women are the oppressed class and rejects the claim that women oppress men, so equal attention for men's disadvantage is not a priority.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Violence is described as the enforcement of male dominance over women, so claims of symmetry are rejected.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Not addressed; universal liberation claims suggest rejecting cultural exemptions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The movement treats armed institutions as male power, so a political guardian role is opposed.

paid-care-work.rationale: The manifesto names domestic work as part of women's exploitation, and recognizing it as labor follows.

filial-duty.rationale: Family duty norms are part of the family institution radical feminists criticize; inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil service recruitment is not discussed in the sources.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Foreign ownership of strategic firms is not discussed in the sources.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Marriage is seen as an oppressive institution perpetuating the sex-role system, so freedom to leave without proof of fault follows.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The manifesto stresses internal democracy and accountability; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not addressed; inferred concern for women's unpaid care years, which private accounts penalize.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land tenure theory is not discussed in the sources on radical feminism.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Budget procedure is not discussed in the sources used.

single-official-language.rationale: Language policy is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land purchase by foreigners is not discussed in the sources.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Radical feminists focus on systemic outcomes, but the sources do not take up racial disparate impact.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from critique of commercial sexualization of women.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not addressed; domination by force is condemned.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from criticism of commercial pornography and sex industries, which MacKinnon calls trafficking.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Foreign funding rules for NGOs are not discussed in the sources on the movement.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Reproductive freedom free from pressure from authorities is a core demand, so state incentives to have children cut against it.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local property purchase limits are not discussed in the sources.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from concern about women as cheap labor.

democratic-peace.rationale: The democratic peace thesis is not discussed in the sources on radical feminism.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Not addressed; adherents both use law and see it as male-made.

non-intervention.rationale: Sovereignty norms are not discussed in the sources used.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The manifesto rejects scapegoating and calls for solidarity with all women; conspiracy claims about minorities are inconsistent with this.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage is listed with the family as an institution to be destroyed, per Wikipedia's account of The Feminists, though not every strand agrees.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from honesty and openness emphasis; not stated.

local-production.rationale: Localist economics is not discussed in the sources on radical feminism.

informal-organisation.rationale: Early radical feminist groups organized as small leaderless consciousness-raising groups with internal democracy.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The relation of national to international law is not discussed in the sources.

religious-nation.rationale: A nation defined by religion draws on male-led religious institutions the movement rejects.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Not addressed; ritual submission is hierarchy.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Regional fiscal policy is not discussed in the sources.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The sources do not discuss the distinction between personal and productive property.

defeat-communism.rationale: Not addressed; radical feminists critique both capitalist and left male-led movements without joining anti-communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Provider mix in public services is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

religion-illusion.rationale: The sources show opposition to religion as male institution, but not the Marxist theory that it fades with material change; split.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Not addressed; capitalism is said to be an extension of male supremacy.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Early politicos saw capitalism as the main source of oppression while radical feminists put male supremacy first; both hold economic change is not enough alone, but many want it, so a moderate yes.

socialized-care.rationale: Early radicals saw the nuclear family as oppressive and Firestone-type thought favors collective childcare; the movement is not unanimous.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Linguistic purism is not discussed in the sources.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaty rights of nations within a state are not discussed in the sources used.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Separatist communities and collective groups exist in the strand, yet not as mainstream program.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred: displacement of minorities is male-supremacist domination.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: A third-way economic course is not discussed in the sources, and radical feminists put sex before economic systems.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Competing claims to land are not discussed in the sources on radical feminism.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Rejecting well-documented atrocity denial follows from the manifesto's honesty standard; no feminist source takes this up.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Radical lesbians treat lesbianism as resistance to compulsory heterosexuality, and radical-cultural feminists promote it as liberating.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Suppression is domination; the manifesto demands internal democracy.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Criticism of male-led religion, including leaving the Church in protest, is part of the movement.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Imperialism is described as an extension of male supremacy.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not addressed; religious armed obligation is unfavored.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Religious-law rule over women is at odds with the movement's aims.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The manifesto and early groups stress internal democracy and ordinary women deciding for themselves.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Radical feminists say male supremacy is the base oppression with others as extensions, yet women of color criticized the movement for neglecting race; adherents are divided.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The movement is divided on this: some such as MacKinnon recognize trans women, while gender-critical radicals like Raymond, Daly, Jeffreys oppose; the historic emphasis on sex-class leans against.

assisted-dying.rationale: End-of-life policy is not discussed in the sources, and adherents are not united on it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The manifesto rejects existing ideologies yet speaks of male supremacy as the root; a claim of obsolescence is not made.

alienated-labor.rationale: Women's exploitation as domestic workers and cheap labor is named, so alienated labor resonates; the Marxist concept itself is not used.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred: the movement opposes generalizing about whole groups, though it criticizes patriarchal religion.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary institutions are not addressed in the sources.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Firestone's aim of eliminating the sex distinction and the manifesto's naming of women as domestic workers imply ending the sexual division of labor, but not all division of labor.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Not addressed; only the anti-capitalist strands would sympathize.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Firestone-style radical-libertarians favor technology to free women from reproduction, whereas radical-cultural feminists distrust it; split.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from distrust of male-built institutions.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from solidarity with all women and the movement's own multicultural critique.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not addressed in the sources, so no stance is documented.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Cattle protection is not discussed in the sources on radical feminism.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Party bans are outside what the sources attribute to radical feminists.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury is not a topic in the sources on radical feminism.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred from the wages-for-housework tradition and concern for women's economic dependence; not in the sources.

bound-labor.rationale: Legally bound labor is a hierarchy of domination of the kind the manifesto opposes.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The manifesto names imperialism an extension of male supremacy, but does not say capitalism inevitably causes great-power war.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Radical feminists fought censorship by building women's presses, though they target pornography as subordination rather than on moral grounds, so moral-virtue censorship is opposed.

church-by-bishops.rationale: A male-led hierarchical church is the model of male institution the movement criticized.

civilizational-union.rationale: Political unions of nations sharing a civilization are outside the movement's documented concerns.

class-collaboration.rationale: The manifesto speaks in class-conflict terms about men and women, and rejects collaboration with oppressors.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The manifesto says male supremacy is the oldest, most basic form of domination, placing sex class before economic class.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by senior male clergy contradicts women's liberation as the movement understands it.

collective-farming.rationale: Agricultural organization is not discussed in the sources.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The sources do not discuss reparations; imperialism appears only as an extension of male supremacy in the manifesto.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Competition and domination are the male-supremacist values the movement opposes; the manifesto asks for solidarity among women.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; militarism is a male domain, so conscription is inferred as opposed, especially for women.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The manifesto stresses internal democracy and women's self-determination.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed; state-imposed hierarchy is distrusted.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The movement grew from civil rights activism, and its manifesto calls for solidarity with the poorest women and rejecting privilege.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism is a Marxist-Leninist idea absent from the sources on radical feminism.

democracy-best.rationale: Inferred from internal democracy and women's self-organizing; its attitude to voters choosing badly is unstated.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora citizenship rights are not covered by the sources on the movement.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The manifesto rejects existing ideologies and hierarchy; not specifically addressed.

direct-action.rationale: Radical feminist action included speakouts, public confessions and campaigns outside electoral politics.

direct-votes.rationale: Referendums versus representatives are not discussed, though the movement values internal democracy, which gives no clear direction.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Racial hierarchy is opposed through solidarity across women and rejection of dividing privilege.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The manifesto's aim is to end male supremacy, and per Wikipedia radical feminists challenge gender roles and Firestone sought to eliminate the sex distinction.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Inferred from solidarity with the poorest women and women's unpaid labor; not discussed.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Inconsistent with solidarity across all women, especially the poorest, though the sources do not discuss cohesion.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-Western coalitions are not addressed in the sources on the movement.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; some ecofeminist radicals support it, but the sources give no position.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Duty-first communitarianism would bind women to roles; the manifesto demands women need not change themselves.

economic-freedom.rationale: The sources do not discuss the link between economic and political freedom as a general claim.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy about minorities is inconsistent with solidarity across women.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred from suspicion of state power, which the manifesto calls a tool of oppression.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The sources say nothing about the UN or global governance, so there is no documented stance.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Alliance policy is not discussed in the sources used for this profile.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Women are said to be oppressed and not to blame, and the demand is equal standing; this is the premise of the movement.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Inferred from class analysis of sex oppression; the sources do not name outcomes.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Ethnic exclusivity is a hierarchical ideology; inferred from solidarity with all women.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed; the movement stresses collective voice and consciousness.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy production is not addressed in the sources on the movement.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Energy policy is not addressed in the manifesto, the Wikipedia account or the Stanford entries.

experts-over-public.rationale: The manifesto starts from personal experience and rejects existing ideologies as male supremacist culture, which places expertise below women's own knowledge.

force-without-un.rationale: Not addressed; militarism is a male domain.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Domination of women by men as a class, whether or not exercised in each case, is the central radical feminist claim about patriarchy.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from concern with cheap female labor.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Wikipedia says radical feminists challenge gender roles and see gender as socialized, and Firestone sought to eliminate the sex distinction; radical-cultural strands partly dissent on the biological side.

gradual-change.rationale: The manifesto refuses to judge actions as reformist or revolutionary and calls for ending male supremacy, not for respecting established institutions, which are called tools of the oppressor.

harm-principle.rationale: MacKinnon and Dworkin argued pornography subordinates women, a harm beyond the narrow liberal view, so the principle is partly contested, but they argue in harm terms.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The structure of executive command over the armed forces is not discussed in the sources.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Biological hierarchy is rejected in line with the movement's socialization view of sex difference and solidarity.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: State control over reproduction runs against reproductive rights free from pressure by authorities.

human-enhancement.rationale: Radical-libertarian strands favor technological liberation from biology, radical-cultural strands critique transformation of bodies; the sources show a divide.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Radical feminist texts do not take a position on armed intervention abroad, and adherents split between anti-militarism and concern for women's rights.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous land rights are not discussed in the sources used, so no common view can be documented.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The movement treats women as a class and MacKinnon's civil rights ordinance is group-based, so rights are not only individual.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Radical-cultural strands such as Daly's critique industry and technology, but others celebrate it; split.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not addressed in libertarian terms; radical feminists condemn male violence against women but do not use this property-based principle.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Radical feminist sources do not take a stance on Israel, and adherents differ on it.

land-value-tax.rationale: Tax design of this kind is outside anything the sources attribute to radical feminism.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Religion is called a male institution, and women left the Church in protest; scripture-based law is incompatible with the movement.

limit-growth.rationale: The sources do not discuss economic growth or the environment, so no stance is documented.

limit-population.rationale: Reproductive choice free from pressure is the demand, so state-limited population conflicts with it, though contraception access is supported.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization rules are not addressed in the sources.

means-match-ends.rationale: The manifesto and early groups practiced internal democracy and leaderless organization as the model of the society wanted.

media-academia-power.rationale: Not addressed; radical feminists critique media, yet not as outranking elected officials.

military-superiority.rationale: Not addressed; militarism is treated as male domination.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary male rule is the opposite of the movement's aims.

national-mission.rationale: Imperialism is called an extension of male supremacy.

national-rebirth.rationale: Rebirth myths typically restore male-ordered hierarchy; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Nationhood is not discussed in the sources, and the manifesto's class unit is women across nations.

nation-first.rationale: Not addressed; solidarity is with all women across borders.

natural-rulers.rationale: The manifesto rejects the claim that women are to blame for subordination and calls male supremacy domination, not nature.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Ecofeminist strands say yes, but the central sources do not address it.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Inferred: radical feminists seek laws and state protection against rape and exploitation.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The manifesto rejects existing ideologies as products of male supremacist culture and starts from women's experience as knowledge.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religion is condemned as a male institution that confines women, so state schools should not instruct in it.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not discussed in the sources, though the movement values equal participation.

one-party-rule.rationale: Single-party rule is hierarchy; the manifesto demands internal democracy.

open-borders.rationale: Border policy is absent from the sources; the call to solidarity with all women gives no direction on migration law.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation through families and traditional bodies would entrench male-headed units, which the movement opposes.

party-commands-army.rationale: Militarized party control is male domination.

party-controls-media.rationale: Radical feminists fought censorship by building women-run presses and distrusted state control of speech.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The movement practiced leaderless internal democracy and rejects binding hierarchy.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The manifesto states that male supremacy is the oldest, most basic form of domination and that all men benefit; Wikipedia describes society as patriarchy in which men dominate women.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Personal oaths between lords and followers are a male-ordered hierarchy.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Not addressed in these terms; the manifesto calls institutions tools of the oppressor, but is more focused on men as a class.

political-violence-never.rationale: Early groups embraced separatism and confrontation but not documented violence; adherents split.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The EU and supranational integration are not discussed in the sources.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Women's oppression and institutions are named as causes of hardship, not population.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of a minority contradicts bodily and collective self-determination and solidarity.

positive-liberty.rationale: Reproductive rights are described as including childcare provisions and freedom from pressure, which implies material means to act on freedom.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Not addressed; cultural traditions are seen as vehicles of male supremacy.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price regulation of food is not covered by the sources.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The manifesto urges women to identify with all women, especially the poorest.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Private force and justice would favor those with power; inferred from the movement's class view.

production-for-use.rationale: Anti-capitalist radical feminists would agree, but the central texts do not discuss production.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Early politicos saw capitalism as the main oppression while radical feminists put male supremacy first; adherents disagree.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not discussed in the sources used.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The movement grew from civil rights activism and the manifesto calls for solidarity across women and rejection of privilege.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Radical-cultural feminists celebrate intuition and the personal, while others critique religion; split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from solidarity with all women.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of privilege; not stated.

restore-past-order.rationale: The goal is ending male supremacy, the oldest order; restoration of past social order is the opposite.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred; the movement criticizes religion but supports individual freedom from male control.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Not addressed; inferred sympathy for workers.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The manifesto judges action by whether it is good for women, which is a results test, but the movement is strongly ideological.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Some radical-cultural writing romanticizes pre-patriarchal life, but this is not a central program.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not a radical feminist topic in the sources.

revolution-justified.rationale: The manifesto aims at final liberation from male supremacy and says actions are judged by what is good for women, not whether revolutionary or reformist.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public housing sales are not discussed in the sources on the movement.

right-to-secede.rationale: Secession is not addressed in the sources on the movement.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not addressed; moral example from male rulers is hierarchy.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cultural institutions as a topic are absent from the sources, though radical feminists criticize male-made culture generally.

school-vouchers.rationale: School funding mechanisms are not discussed in the sources on the movement.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from the manifesto's claim that violence enforces oppression; accountability not discussed.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The manifesto emphasizes solidarity with all women, though it tells women to do what is good for women.

separate-church-state.rationale: Religion is seen as a male institution, so separating it from the state fits; not a stated program.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional checks and balances are not discussed in the sources used.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The sources do not apply the concept of settler colonialism, and adherents have no shared line.

single-common-good.rationale: The manifesto treats women's and men's interests as opposed class interests, which rejects a single common good.

socialism-one-country.rationale: This Marxist-Leninist debate lies outside the sources, which treat male supremacy as the main target.

socialized-markets.rationale: Radical feminist sources do not discuss worker or public ownership within markets, so adherents have no common view.

state-as-business.rationale: Not addressed; commercial logic applied to people is disfavored given critique of buying and selling women.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The manifesto calls institutions tools of the oppressors, but the oppressing class is men, not capitalists, so the claim in class-instrument form is split.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Industrial policy is not a topic in the sources, so no position is documented.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Socialist state-building theory is not addressed in the sources, where states are seen as tools of oppression.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Trade protection is not discussed in the sources on the movement.

taxation-theft.rationale: Radical feminists look to the state to protect and provide for women; the claim is inconsistent with that.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from rejection of hereditary privilege; not stated.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Firestone-style faith in technology versus radical-cultural suspicion; split.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Imperialism is named an extension of male supremacy.

total-state.rationale: The movement distrusts institutions as tools of the oppressor and prizes women's autonomy.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade balance policy is not discussed in the sources.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from distrust of state institutions; not stated.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Women's equal rights under one law would remove religious personal laws that subordinate women; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: The sources do not address moral epistemology; adherents hold universal claims on women's rights yet criticize inherited ideology.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed; prolonged leader power is distrusted.

vanguard-party.rationale: The manifesto makes consciousness-raising among women the main task and rejects existing ideologies and hierarchies; a leading party is opposed.

war-builds-character.rationale: War is a male domain; the movement condemns violence as enforcement of domination.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; solidarity with the poorest women implies no citizen-only limits.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The sources do not address how property should be distributed among owners.

workers-councils.rationale: Not addressed; some anarcha- and socialist strands favor them.

workers-nation.rationale: The manifesto calls on women to identify with all women, which suggests transnational solidarity.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Women's unpaid domestic work is named as labor, so compulsory paid-work conditions would penalize carers; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from democratic and anti-hierarchy principles.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Radical feminism sees organised religion as an instrument of patriarchal power and rejects authority justified by divine order.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Adherents split between seeing veiling as patriarchal control and opposing state bans; the sources do not settle it.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Treating sexual harassment as male domination of women, radical feminists would want such claims heard in public; inferred, not discussed in the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Many radical feminists are anti-capitalist yet the strand has no settled economic model; adherents are split.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Militarism is criticised as masculinist by many, but abolition is not a common demand and adherents differ; inferred.

rich-first.rationale: The manifesto stresses solidarity with the poorest women, which cuts against leaving some behind first; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Great-power blocs are not a radical feminist concern and the strand has no settled view.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary male-line power is a patriarchal institution in the radical view, but succession as such is not discussed in the sources.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Banking structure is not addressed; radical feminists focus on sex-class rather than credit institutions.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The sources do not address international lenders, and radical feminism is not defined by a position on state economic policy.

property-franchise.rationale: A property qualification would entrench the power of men as a class, which radical feminism opposes; inferred from its analysis of patriarchy.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Radical-cultural strands and ecofeminist currents link the two, but the core view treats sex-class domination as primary; contested among strands.

reification.rationale: Radical feminists criticised Marxism for treating class as basic and sex as secondary, so they would not adopt this class-economy framing; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Radical feminists attack male control of media and pornography more than wealth as such; the sources do not address the claim.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Strands split on the state and law, with some seeking legal reform and others seeing law as patriarchal; no source settles it.

racial-franchise.rationale: Radical feminism opposes hierarchies of domination, which it sees as extensions of sex-class, so a racial franchise is rejected.

online-participation.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; strands favour autonomous women's organising in various forms.

open-government-data.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and not a radical feminist concern.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Radical feminism treats marriage as an oppressive institution and opposes the state or religion controlling women's choices.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Targeting a minority's shops is not a radical feminist tactic and conflicts with opposition to domination; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not addressed; autonomous women-only consciousness-raising groups are favoured over mixed deliberative bodies, but the sources say nothing on sortition.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Radical feminists criticise religion as patriarchal, with some favouring reinterpretation and others rejection; inferred, not sourced.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Radical feminism centres sex-class rather than economic class, but opposes concentrated hierarchical power generally; inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Radical feminists are anti-militarist and split on the military and on gender identity politics; no common position.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Radical feminists criticise organised religion as patriarchal but did not call for state-imposed atheism; inferred.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: MacKinnon and Dworkin sought stronger legal enforcement against sexual violence, though some strands are abolitionist; inferred from the legal strand.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed by radical feminism, which treats sex as the primary division; no stance can be inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Radical feminism treats poverty among women as structural and demands institutional change rather than charity; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed by radical feminism and no common view can be inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not addressed; autonomous women's organising favours direct participation but no stance on delegation exists.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed by radical feminism; some ecofeminist strands care about it, but there is no common view.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Radical feminists see religion as patriarchal and demand women's equality in all institutions, though many reject reform of religion as futile.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Radical feminists regard marriage as a patriarchal institution to be abolished, so mere sharing of authority is a partial agreement at best.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not addressed in the sources and adherents have no common line; inferred as neutral.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the left, anti-exploitation orientation and concern for poor women in the Redstockings Manifesto; not a stated position.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed and adherents are split; no stated position.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Autonomous, anti-hierarchical organizing and opposition to male dominance make drilled national youth movements alien; inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from the movement's opposition to militarism as a male-dominated institution; not stated.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from its concern with violence against a subordinated group; not stated.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's solidarity with the poorest women and opposition to exploitation; not a defining issue.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The movement supports women's right to defend themselves against male violence; inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Nationalist myth is not part of its analysis, which treats sex class as primary; inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Strands split: Firestone-style radical-libertarians treat even the sex distinction as removable, while gender-critical radical feminists hold sex is biological (s4).

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Redstockings and radical feminism treat women as an oppressed class with shared interests (s1), so politics can rest on that category, though trans-inclusive strands dispute it.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Honouring national martyrs belongs to male-dominated nationalism, which it opposes; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Politics is framed as class struggle between sexes, not spiritual struggle, although the cultural strand has spiritual currents; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Radical feminists critique patriarchal religion and many call for non-male God language; inferred, not in the sources.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Judging institutions by their effect on women follows from the patriarchy analysis; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Rejects ethnic hierarchy as an extension of patriarchal domination; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its rejection of ethnonational projects.

independent-unions.rationale: The Redstockings Manifesto treats women as exploited cheap labour, so organisations free of state or party control fit; inferred, not discussed.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Radical feminism holds that sex-based domination is more basic than class, so it would not accept working-class power as the test of a just society; inferred from its priority of sex over class.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from concern for women's access to care and services; sources do not discuss ownership of utilities.

second-chamber.rationale: Legislative structure is not a radical feminist topic.

municipal-property.rationale: Ownership of production is not the movement's focus; it treats the family and sex class as the base of oppression.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Radical feminism favours autonomous women's organising but does not address municipal confederalism.

family-wage.rationale: The manifesto names the family as an institution of male supremacy, so a wage premised on a dependent family reinforces women's dependence; inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Inferred from radical feminist distrust of male-dominated medicine and its risks to women's bodies; the sources do not address drug regulation.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's concern with sex markets does not yield a position on untraceable payments.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not addressed directly; adherents are split between privacy for women and concerns over anonymous abuse and pornography online.

person-over-state.rationale: The radical feminist critique of objectification, that women are treated as means to men's ends, fits the principle that no person is merely a means; the state-serving-person clause is inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Radical-cultural strands embrace goddess spirituality while others are strictly materialist, so adherents are split.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Devolution is not a radical feminist concern.

gm-crops.rationale: Agricultural technology is not within the movement's focus; ecofeminist strands are sceptical, others indifferent.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban planning is not within the movement's focus.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Radical feminism treats sex as the primary class division and women's interests as common across races, so it resists race-based organising as primary; inferred from its priority of sex.

racial-pride.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents differ and it is not central to the theory.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Radical feminists tie militarism to male dominance, so restricting force to defence is a natural inference; not stated in the sources.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Radical feminism treats sex class as the basic division and is internationalist about women; inferred from that, it gives no weight to linguistic nation.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from its view that religion and family are patriarchal institutions; separate religious electorates would entrench them.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Not a radical feminist concern; inferred from its analysis of patriarchy as the main threat, not foreign powers.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from its demand to open institutions to women and its egalitarian aims; the sources do not discuss tuition.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Ecofeminists link domination of women and nature, but the sources do not address market instruments, and adherents are split on them.

future-generations.rationale: Ecofeminist strands stress care for the Earth; the core sources do not address it, so this is inferred.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Strands split: cultural radical feminists celebrate female values of care and nonviolence, while others reject the idea of innate sex differences and seek to abolish gender.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from feminist critiques of militarism as male-dominated; the sources do not discuss disarmament directly.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to hidden male-run power structures; the sources do not discuss diplomacy.

capital-controls.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; anti-capitalist strands might agree but the core is indifferent to the issue.

missingStatements.text: Buying sex should be a criminal offence while selling sex is decriminalized.
missingStatements.rationale: MacKinnon developed this Nordic or Equality Model, which criminalizes buyers, decriminalizes sellers and funds exit support, as the radical feminist abolitionist policy.

missingStatements.text: Heterosexuality is a political institution that sustains male dominance.
missingStatements.rationale: Radical lesbians define heterosexuality as an oppressive political institution and The Feminists listed it with marriage and the family as institutions to destroy.

missingStatements.text: Personal relationships between women and men are political relationships of power.
missingStatements.rationale: The Redstockings Manifesto states that every such relationship is a class relationship and that personal experience is the starting point of analysis.

notes: Strands differ: radical-libertarian feminists (Firestone, Millett) seek to abolish gender and favor technology, radical-cultural feminists (Daly) celebrate femaleness and distrust it. Trans-inclusive radical feminists such as MacKinnon differ from gender-critical ones such as Raymond and Jeffreys, so the gender-identity answer is a contested majority-of-historical-texts call.
